title: PortfolioOwnershipRatchet
description: Machine-readable portfolio own-when-proven / day-0 ownership budget contract. This reconciles SOURCE Class A/B/C and LINUX OWN_DAY0/OWN_EARLY/DEFER_VENDORED/PERMANENT_REUSE rubrics into one capacity gate so Oyatie cannot silently turn per-component own-when-proven doctrine into an unbounded simultaneous from-scratch substrate program.

_meta.source_request: ARCH-OWN-RATCHET-001: author a portfolio ownership ratchet / day-0 budget contract from the hyperscaler build-vs-buy audits.
non_goals: Do not re-litigate every ADR in this contract.
Do not block narrow implementation lanes that do not introduce a new ownership claim.
Do not add or modify generated faces; generated JSON remains materialized by the existing cloud-ci/generated-face pipeline.
Do not create new legacy oya CLI merge authority; enforcement must land through cloud-ci/Rust gate packets behind oya-ci-required when implemented.

source_authorities.role: discoverability hub; this contract must be reachable from entry_points
operating contract until explicit PHASE-5 promotion evidence promotes /specs/agent-operating-contract.json
sequencing, plain-git/cloud-ci authority, and first-deliverable guardrails
shared claim alignment lock and serialization policy
readiness/mechanical-enforcement claim ceilings and evidence vocabulary
primary audit evidence for the missing portfolio-level day-0 ownership budget
primary audit evidence that questionable decisions share an own-day-0 vs own-when-proven trigger-threshold pattern

OWN_DAY0.source_equivalent: Class A / in-house obligatory only when the owned surface is the narrow differentiator and cannot be safely isolated behind a port
OWN_DAY0.meaning: Oyatie builds and carries the owned implementation from the first committed delivery window.
OWN_DAY0.claim_ceiling_until_gate_lands: spec_ready; not mechanically_enforced and not production_ready

OWN_EARLY.source_equivalent: Class B / value-anchored trigger with owned port or overlay now and engine/control-plane ownership after proof
OWN_EARLY.meaning: Oyatie owns the seam, adapter, policy overlay, or differentiating slice now; the commodity engine remains vendored until numeric triggers fire.
OWN_EARLY.claim_ceiling_until_trigger_fires: target_non_claim or spec_ready for destination ownership; implementation may claim port/overlay ownership only

DEFER_VENDORED.source_equivalent: Class B vendored-now / adopt proven OSS behind a port
DEFER_VENDORED.meaning: A proven OSS or managed substrate is the day-0 implementation. Oyatie owns the port, contract, and exit path, not the engine.
DEFER_VENDORED.claim_ceiling: may claim reusable substrate, portability, and exit-readiness; may not claim owned engine/control-plane

PERMANENT_REUSE.source_equivalent: Class C / no differentiation upside or external standard must remain canonical
PERMANENT_REUSE.meaning: The external standard or OSS dependency is a durable platform choice. Oyatie owns configuration, policy, support, and upgrade discipline, not a replacement program.
PERMANENT_REUSE.claim_ceiling: reuse/support claim only; replacement claims require a new ratchet amendment

portfolio_day0_budget.major_ownership_bet_definition: A from-scratch or first-party replacement of a proven substrate/control plane/engine that is expected to consume more than 12 engineer-months, creates a new public or internal platform surface, or must carry hyperscaler-grade correctness, durability, security, scheduling, identity, workflow, data, networking, or operations semantics.

preauthorized_small_OWN_DAY0_scope.scope: Cedar policy semantics and app-authz contract surface
preauthorized_small_OWN_DAY0_scope.source: LINUX ADR-0020 / SOURCE ADR-0007, ADR-0243, ADR-0211 as cited by the audits
preauthorized_small_OWN_DAY0_scope.limit: The Cedar contract may be day-0; a compile-to-Rust engine replacement still consumes the major slot unless explicitly reclassified by founder decision.

preauthorized_small_OWN_DAY0_scope.scope: core kernel crates that are purely Oyatie domain boundaries, ports, schemas, or policy wrappers
preauthorized_small_OWN_DAY0_scope.source: LINUX ADR-0020 small day-0 set referenced by build-vs-buy audit line 21
preauthorized_small_OWN_DAY0_scope.limit: This exception does not cover replacing commodity engines such as databases, Kubernetes control-plane components, workflow engines, DCIM, native client fleets, or build engines.

budget_exceedance_requires: named numeric forcing function that has already fired or an explicit founder override
headcount and runway capacity model for every active major slot
portfolio opportunity-cost table naming which other OWN_DAY0 candidates move to OWN_EARLY or DEFER_VENDORED
cloud-ci/Rust gate proposal with known-BAD and known-GOOD fixtures
rollback or vendored fallback plan for every exceeded slot
portfolio_day0_budget.default_when_evidence_is_missing: DEFER_VENDORED behind a port, or OWN_EARLY for the narrow differentiating overlay only.

claim_ceilings.new_OWN_DAY0_claim_without_budget_slot: forbidden; candidate change must downgrade to target_non_claim or DEFER_VENDORED until a budget slot and founder/risk evidence exist
claim_ceilings.own_when_proven_destination_claim: allowed only as target_non_claim unless the trigger has fired and replacement parity evidence is present
claim_ceilings.mechanically_enforced_claim: forbidden until a branch-protected cloud-ci/Rust gate with RED/GREEN fixtures is wired into oya-ci-required per /specs/hyperscaler-production-readiness-claim-contract.json
claim_ceilings.production_or_hyperscaler_grade_claim: not granted by this contract; use /specs/hyperscaler-production-readiness-claim-contract.json evidence domains

decision_mappings.current_risk: legitimate differentiator but too large to run alongside multiple other from-scratch substrates
decision_mappings.default_bucket: OWN_EARLY unless founder allocates the single major OWN_DAY0 slot
decision_mappings.budget_effect: Consumes the one major OWN_DAY0 slot if selected as crown jewel; otherwise own datastore/differentiator seams behind retained Postgres+Citus and other workload stores.
decision_mappings.founder_call_question: Is cloud-data the single crown-jewel day-0 substrate, with Kubernetes/control-plane/container/workflow/DCIM/node-OS/client breadth re-sequenced behind it?

decision_mappings.current_risk: rewriting apiserver/scheduler/controller-manager day-0 overreaches the AWS/Azure EKS/AKS pattern
decision_mappings.default_bucket: OWN_EARLY for cellular + owned datastore seam; DEFER_VENDORED for upstream Kubernetes control-plane components
decision_mappings.budget_effect: Full Rust control-plane rewrite consumes the major OWN_DAY0 slot if founder insists; cellular/datastore seam alone does not.
decision_mappings.founder_call_question: Is the moat the cellular/owned-datastore substrate under a Kubernetes-compatible port, or a full Rust apiserver/scheduler/controller rewrite?
required_trigger_or_evidence: upstream k8s control plane cannot meet declared cell scale

decision_mappings.surface: L0-L8 container platform and L7 build engine
decision_mappings.current_risk: L7 BuildKit-class build engine is a separable second mountain
decision_mappings.default_bucket: OWN_EARLY for isolation/runtime/content-store spine; DEFER_VENDORED for L7 build engine behind BuildKit/Buildah port
decision_mappings.budget_effect: Owning L7 day-0 consumes or competes for the major slot; keeping L7 vendored preserves budget for a crown-jewel substrate.
decision_mappings.founder_call_question: Does the founder explicitly allocate day-0 ownership to the L7 build engine, or defer it behind a BuildKit/Buildah port?
required_trigger_or_evidence: BuildKit/Buildah fails a named supply-chain/performance/isolation requirement

decision_mappings.current_risk: day-0 durable-execution engine ownership skips the Temporal-class proof gate unless the Temporal bridge and parity gate stay explicit
decision_mappings.default_bucket: DEFER_VENDORED Temporal-class durable-execution substrate during the bridge period; OWN_EARLY per-tenant versioning, jurisdiction overlay, autonomy-ceiling layer, and SDK/port shim; destination oya-workflow engine is Tier-3 bespoke after durable-execution parity
decision_mappings.budget_effect: No day-0 major slot is allocated to the workflow engine. ADR-0482 founder authority places oya-workflow in the Tier-3 bespoke substrate roadmap with Temporal parallel-run and an SDK shim until durable-execution parity is proven.
decision_mappings.founder_call_resolution: Resolved by ADR-0482: keep the Temporal-class bridge and own the differentiating workflow overlays now; build/cut over oya-workflow only behind the Tier-3 durable-execution parity gate.
required_trigger_or_evidence: Temporal bridge or equivalent durable-execution substrate selected

decision_mappings.current_risk: DCIM day-0 precedes physical data-center ownership; permanent no-silicon language overstates the correct Phase-3 founder-ratification escape hatch
decision_mappings.default_bucket: DEFER_VENDORED or OSS DCIM behind cohesion ports until owned colo/physical DC Phase-2; own DCIM at W-DataCenter-Operations when physical capacity exists at scale; commercial silicon remains the default and custom data-center silicon is prohibited unless a Phase-3+ forcing function plus founder ratification reopens it
decision_mappings.budget_effect: No day-0 major slot is allocated to DCIM. Future in-house DCIM waits for owned physical or colocated DC capacity; custom silicon remains anti-scope by default with only a Phase-3+ founder-ratified revisit if commercial silicon/RFP options fail.
decision_mappings.founder_call_resolution: Resolved by the long-horizon DC operations authority already in PRD/DESIGN plus ADR-0032's founder-ratification escape hatch: do not build DCIM day-0; do not treat no-custom-silicon as an unchangeable eternal law, but require a Phase-3+ forcing function and founder ratification before any silicon exception.
required_trigger_or_evidence: owned physical or colocated DC capacity
Phase-3+ silicon forcing function plus founder ratification if commercial silicon fails

decision_mappings.surface: developer portal IDP vs OIDC identity provider IdP
decision_mappings.current_risk: naming collision can smuggle identity-provider ownership through developer-portal wording unless Internal Developer Platform portal/BFF scope and ADR-0476 OIDC identity-provider authority stay explicitly separated
decision_mappings.default_bucket: Internal Developer Platform portal/BFF aggregation stays separate from OIDC identity-provider authority and does not allocate or imply OIDC identity-provider ownership here; OIDC identity provider follows ADR-0476 with a Phase-1 Keycloak bridge and a founder-accepted oya-identity bespoke Rust target after feature parity; Zitadel is superseded by current identity authority
decision_mappings.budget_effect: Bespoke OIDC issuer ownership is an explicit founder-accepted identity roadmap item, not an implication of the developer-portal IDP naming collision. The bridge remains Keycloak until oya-identity feature parity and integration gates pass.
decision_mappings.founder_call_resolution: Resolved for OIDC identity authority by ADR-0476 and ADR-0482: Internal Developer Platform portal/BFF wording and OIDC identity-provider authority are separate; the OIDC provider does not stay on Zitadel until the old ADR-0211 ≥50K-tenant trigger, because ADR-0476 founder-locks oya-identity with Keycloak as the Phase-1 bridge.
required_trigger_or_evidence: Keycloak Phase-1 bridge and traffic shadowing

decision_mappings.surface: flat vertical catalog as owned first-party microservices
decision_mappings.current_risk: architecture structure is sound but day-0 breadth resembles many vertical SaaS companies at once
decision_mappings.default_bucket: OWN_EARLY substrate + cohesion layer; DEFER_VENDORED/PARTNER for vertical product breadth until selected by product/market forcing function
decision_mappings.budget_effect: Each first-party vertical does not consume the substrate slot individually, but unbounded day-0 breadth violates portfolio capacity and must serialize behind FD-001 exit evidence.
decision_mappings.founder_call_question: Is day-0 scope the substrate/cohesion layer with incremental or partner verticals, or are medical/pharmacy/banking/insurance/manufacturing/logistics first-party day-0 product builds?

decision_mappings.surface: five fully-native client stacks per product
decision_mappings.current_risk: five native stacks multiplies parity and team load before product proof
decision_mappings.default_bucket: DEFER_VENDORED or staged native expansion; day-0 web plus one strategic native client unless founder allocates explicit scope
decision_mappings.budget_effect: Client-stack breadth is a portfolio capacity slot, not the substrate OWN_DAY0 slot; it still requires founder scope ruling before day-0 commitment.
decision_mappings.founder_call_question: Commit to five fully-native clients day-0, or web + one native day-0 with other clients deferred behind OpenAPI contracts?

decision_mappings.surface: bespoke Rust oya-ci / Prow-shaped CI platform
decision_mappings.current_risk: direction is hyperscaler-aligned but day-0 ownership may precede Argo Workflows/cloud-ci bridge insufficiency evidence
decision_mappings.default_bucket: OWN_EARLY destination; DEFER_VENDORED/bridge for orchestration pieces until lane-count, latency, isolation, or vendor-quota triggers fire
decision_mappings.budget_effect: Full bespoke CI control-plane day-0 competes for the major slot unless treated as an accepted founder exception with its own capacity model.
decision_mappings.founder_call_question: Is oya-ci a day-0 founder-locked exception, or gated behind lane count / gate latency / Argo Workflows insufficiency evidence?

decision_mappings.current_risk: Cedar contract is aligned; owned compiler/evaluator day-0 is a trigger-threshold question
decision_mappings.default_bucket: OWN_EARLY compiler/evaluator behind adopted Cedar contract; OWN_DAY0 only for policy semantics/contract surface unless founder exception
decision_mappings.budget_effect: Owned compiler/evaluator day-0 consumes the major slot if it replaces the adopted Cedar engine immediately.
decision_mappings.founder_call_question: Is Cedar the long-term engine with Oyatie overlays, or a vendored adapter pending a day-0 compile-to-Rust owned engine?

decision_mappings.current_risk: the staged ladder is healthy, but SOURCE Talos adoption and LINUX Rust node-OS cannot both be day-0 canonical implementations
decision_mappings.default_bucket: DEFER_VENDORED actual Talos day-0; OWN_EARLY Rust node-OS behind beat-or-parity scorecard
decision_mappings.budget_effect: Rust node-OS as immediate replacement consumes a major slot; Talos-compatible port/scorecard does not.
decision_mappings.founder_call_question: Adopt actual Talos day-0 and treat Rust node-OS as OWN_EARLY, or allocate day-0 ownership to Rust node-OS as the canonical node implementation?

gate_proposal.trigger: Any candidate PR that adds or amends ADR/spec/masterplan language containing OWN_DAY0, own day-0, own from scratch, bespoke engine, replace proven substrate, or equivalent ownership-escalation claims.

checks.rule: A new major OWN_DAY0 claim must reference an allocated portfolio_day0_budget slot or an explicit founder exception record.
OWN_EARLY escalation must cite a numeric trigger, sustained measurement window, and replacement parity evidence.
A planned gate or local check may not claim mechanically_enforced until the cloud-ci/Rust gate is branch-protected and RED/GREEN fixtures are proven.
If budget or trigger evidence is absent, the candidate language must say DEFER_VENDORED or target_non_claim rather than OWN_DAY0.
The gate must fail closed if the ownership-ratchet change hand-edits any *.generated.json.

founder_call_followups.policy: Create blocked, human-only Kanban cards only for decision groups where founder judgment changes the allowed day-0 scope. Implementation workers should not infer these choices from audit prose.

groups.reason: Only the founder can choose or override the single major day-0 ownership slot when several legitimate but mutually competing infrastructure moats exist.
Vertical breadth and native-client breadth are product/portfolio scope decisions, not architecture-only conclusions.
Workflow-engine, DCIM, silicon anti-scope, and identity-provider timing needed founder judgment because they set long-lived ownership commitments across regulated/runtime operations surfaces.
groups.resolution: Resolved for t_1b9b3e63 by reconciling BVB-06/BVB-07/BVB-08 decision_mappings to ADR-0482, ADR-0476, and the long-horizon DC operations authority. Source ADR/doc amendment work remains queued separately where older prose still conflicts.

worker_guidance.default_action_for_new_questionable_owne: Downgrade to DEFER_VENDORED behind a port or OWN_EARLY overlay until a founder card resolves the budget/trigger question.
safe_to_continue_without_founder_call: Adding a port/adapter around an already selected OSS substrate
Documenting trigger evidence without escalating ownership
Narrow implementation that does not introduce a new ownership claim
Vocabulary amendments that align retired terms without changing build-vs-buy posture
must_block_or_create_founder_call_card: Allocating a new major OWN_DAY0 slot
Changing a DEFER_VENDORED engine into a day-0 owned engine
Committing all listed verticals or all native clients as day-0 first-party scope
